attributes.residual: 40 real rows at count parity 125/125, multiset DIFFERS by target-only +1 addi +1 li against ours-only -2 lwz -- a BALANCED, compensating baseline, which is why it scores far better than any half-fix. DIAGNOSIS, confirmed and worth keeping: our two ours-only `lwz` rows are ALIAS-FORCED RELOADS, not sloppy reconstruction. Source lines 3679-3698 write `block->next = mergeNext->next; pool->next = block; if (block->next != NULL)`, and the intervening `pool->next = block;` store may alias `block->next`, so C semantics REQUIRE the re-read; the target does not re-read, so the original source held the loaded pointer in a temp. The two sites are symmetric: ours emits `stw r5,32(r3); lwz r7,4(r5)` at +0x158/+0x15c where target emits `cmplwi r7,0; stw r5,32(r3)` at +0x160/+0x164, and identically at +0x194/+0x198 against target +0x198/+0x19c. All three cures removed both reloads exactly as predicted, landing at 123 instructions -- 2 SHORT of target, because the target's OTHER two words (`addi r10,r8,0` = the mergeNext copy at +0x78, and `li r4,0` at +0xcc) are still missing from our stream. Removing the reloads alone therefore unbalances a compensating baseline and triggers a whole-entry-block reschedule (the `lbl_80128710` lis/addi pair migrates into the prologue), costing +158 to +166 real. The next lane's step 1 is the JOINT probe recorded in `hypothesis`.

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: Run the joint edit and read `fndiff --ops`. If the multiset still reports target-only `+1 addi` after `mergeNext = next;` is moved into the else-arm, then the copy is not source-reachable from that assignment's position and the joint premise is dead in one build.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: no -- the joint form was NOT built this session. The two halves were each measured separately: the reload half was probed three times (all removed the reloads, all regressed), and the `addi r10,r8,0` half was read off the target disassembly at +0x78 and identified as the `mergeNext` copy, but never probed.
hypothesis.statement: The reload removal must be done JOINTLY with recovering the target's two missing words, not alone. Target carries `addi r10,r8,0` at +0x78 -- an explicit copy of `next` into a separate register for `mergeNext`, emitted INSIDE the `next != NULL` arm -- and `li r4,0` at +0xcc on the `prev == NULL` path. Our source assigns `mergeNext = next;` before the `if` (line 3618), where MWCC coalesces it with `next` and emits no copy; moving that assignment into the else-arm should force the copy. Per AGENTS.md residual-work discipline 6, these are two parked variables touching the same instructions and need ONE joint probe: move `mergeNext = next;` into the else-arm AND apply the dead-local reuse of `next` in the two relink blocks in the same edit.
